title: Construct a fully paid original-oracle TV baseline at O(d log^2 d) queries
statement: Set T=.5log(200d),N=ceil(400dT^2),delta=T/N. Draw Y0~N(0,I); for k=0..N-1 query grad V(Yk) once and set Y(k+1)=Yk-delta grad V(Yk)+sqrt(2delta)G(k+1), independent standard Gaussian vectors. The Hessian/mode bounds give KL(N(0,I)||piV)<=d/2. Exact Langevin entropy contracts at rate2, so KL(Law(XT)||piV)<=1/400 and TV<=sqrt(1/800). Euler moments obey E||Yk||^2<=2d and E||grad V(Yk)||^2<=8d. Standard pathwise Girsanov comparison gives KL(Ypath||Xpath)<=dTdelta*(1+8delta/3)<=1/240 since delta<=1/(400dT) and<=1/4. Data processing/Pinsker give discretization TV<=sqrt(1/480); total TV<.081<.1. EVERY run pays exactly N ORIGINAL first-order queries, O(dN) scalar work, d(N+1) Gaussian scalar draws and O(d) memory. No warm distribution, Hessian, normalizer, prox or smoothed-score oracle is used. This is a complete explicit continuous-output ORIGINAL-oracle baseline, but N=Theta(d log^2d) eventually exceeds exp(C log^(1/3)d) for every fixed C. It is not a sharp-scale solution or a finite-bit TV claim.
